This is the homepage for the "Data Science for Transport Planning: from origin-destination to route network datasets" workshop.
It will be delivered as part of the [PhD School](https://mobiletartu.ut.ee/workshops-and-academic-lecture/) that precedes the [Mobile Tartu 2026 conference](https://mobiletartu.ut.ee/).
In it you will learn how to work with these datasets and generate meaningful transport planning-related results. Exercises will stretch more advanced attendees.

It is based on data from the {spanishoddata} [@kotov2026], a package that was conceived during Mobile Tartu 2024, which provides access to a large spatio-temporal dataset of origin-destination (OD) flows in Spain.

## Getting Started

The quickest way to get started is on GitHub Codespaces, which you can launch by clicking the link below:

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/tdscience/tartu26?quickstart=1)

See the [prerequisites](prerequisites.qmd) for more details on how to set up your environment.

## Workshop Workbook

The main practical content is in the [workbook](workbook.qmd).

## Further reading

If you enjoyed this course, you may want to check out some of the links below:

- The [Data Science for Transport Planning website](https://tdscience.github.io/dstp/) with more sessions taught over 2 days.
- The [Transport Data Science](https://itsleeds.github.io/tds) course materials from the University of Leeds, which cover a wider range of topics and datasets.
- The Transportation chapter of [Geocomputation with R](https://r.geocompx.org) book @lovelaceGeocomputation2025, which includes a section on OD data and route networks.
